description_full: EBOS Group Limited engages in the marketing, wholesale, and distribution of healthcare, medical, pharmaceutical, and animal care products in Australia, Southeast Asia, and New Zealand. It operates through the Healthcare and Animal Care segments. The company provides healthcare logistics; medication management solutions; pharmacy management software; pharmacy data, consumer loyalty, and analytics services; and health communications, programs, and consultancy services. It also offers community-based health care services and programs; vitamins, minerals and supplements, herbal and fruit teas, and natural toothpastes, as well as functional foods, including molasses and manuka honey; Pharmacy Choice, a five-step integrated retail program for independent pharmacies; and healthSAVE, a community pharmacy banner that helps members drive their retail businesses. In addition, the company offers healthcare distribution, warehousing, clinical trial management, and product registration services; clinical trial logistics; aesthetic healthcare devices, medical-grade cosmeceuticals, and injectables; dog and cat food, and treats; and surgical devices and medical consumables. Further, it provides pet nutrition, treats, clean-up, and grooming products and accessories; supplies pet medicines and other products to veterinary clinics and specialty retailers; manufactures and supplies dog rolls; and wholesales veterinary products. The company was formerly known as Early Bros Dental & Surgical Supplies Ltd. and changed its name to EBOS Group Limited in 1986. EBOS Group Limited was incorporated in 1922 and is headquartered in Docklands, Australia.

financial_summary: EBOS Group, Ltd. is a mid-cap healthcare business with a $2.4B market cap on $11.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 8% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 13% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The business throws off $231M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.4× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and interest coverage runs at 3.9×.

Shareholder yield of 4.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
